title: Drive straight with the gyro
summary: Correct the heading all the way so the robot really drives straight.

steps.title: Open the starter program
steps.text: The robot drives 80 cm, constantly correcting its direction with the gyro.

steps.title: Why it works
steps.text: Real robots never drive perfectly straight: one wheel is a tiny bit bigger, or slips. The gyro notices the robot pointing off course, and the program steers back. This is another P controller: correction = yaw × 2.

steps.title: Try it 1
steps.text: Set Realism to Challenging. Run ▶×5 with this program and with a plain move 80 cm block. Compare.

steps.title: Try it 2
steps.text: Change the gain 2 to 0.5 and to 6. What happens?

steps.title: Try it 3
steps.text: Use DriveStraight and TurnRight together to make an accurate square.

steps.title: Try it 4
steps.text: The gyro keeps the robot pointing the way it started. If it starts crooked, it drives crooked. How could you line the robot up the same way every time?

steps.title: Take the challenge
steps.text: Start the challenge, then press ▶︎×5. The simulator checks your runs for you.
